answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when a challenge proves coordinated fraud. The stake does not prove a personhood—one attacker can still create many identities—but it makes each Sybil costly: capital is tied up, and detection risks losing it. A lotus, an orchard, or a garden can all be cheap names; none is a substitute for bonded collateral.
